_comment: The build menu's catalogue. Lives beside items.json because a buildable is spent inventory turned into a placed thing, and splitting the two put the cost in one file and the thing it buys in another.
_comment_scope: GAME_DESIGN.md 20 lists a dozen categories (floors, walls, roofs, doors, beds, lights...). One entry ships here on purpose: the menu is the work, and the eleventh entry after this one costs a JSON block and no code.
_comment_camp: GAME_DESIGN.md 20's mandatory tutorial is shelter, bed, campfire, rest. OWNER-0902-CAMP-SPLIT: the opening used to sell that as one bundled `camp` buy (tent + campfire + bedroll, one placement) because 'the smallest thing that lets the sequence exist' read as 'ship it as a single object'. A prior owner playtest (ralph/OWNER-0902-TENT-CAMPFIRE-PLACEMENT) found the real complaint underneath 'can't place the tent and campfire': the menu never told the player it was a bundle at all, and the owner's direct follow-up was blunter than a label fix — split the pieces so each is independently placeable, the way floor/wall/roof/fence already are. `tent`/`campfire`/`bedroll` below are that split; each keeps its own hand-authored placement script (scripts/build/camp_tent.gd, campfire.gd, player_bed.gd) because each still carries positioning/lit-state/interaction beyond a bare mesh, the same reason `camp` itself was never plain geometry.
_comment_cost: TUNABLE. `tent`/`campfire`/`bedroll` sum to the old bundled camp's 12 wood / 8 stone / 10 fiber, split so each piece's cost matches what it visibly is rather than dividing evenly: campfire is mostly stone (the ring) with a little wood (fuel) -- 2 wood / 8 stone; tent is wood-framed canvas -- 6 wood / 4 fiber; bedroll is fiber-heavy bedding on a light wood frame -- 4 wood / 6 fiber. 2+6+4=12 wood, 8 stone, 4+6=10 fiber -- the same total the bundle always cost, not a stealth price hike.
_comment_placement: Nothing here places geometry. Confirming a buildable sets GameState.pending_build, which is the seam the building system reads when M8 gives it one. A build menu that silently did nothing would read as a bug; one that arms a selection is honest about where the work stops.
_comment_pieces: R2.6. `tent`/`campfire`/`bedroll` stay their own hand-authored geometry (scripts/build/camp_tent.gd, campfire.gd, player_bed.gd) because each carries its own sink-compensated positioning, lit state, or rest/craft interaction, not just a mesh. `floor`/`wall`/`roof`/`fence` are plain placeable geometry — no `contains`, no interaction — so `mesh` names the model directly and `scripts/build/build_piece.gd` places any of them generically rather than each needing its own script. `door` (OP21-08) joined the hand-authored side for the same reason: it needs the real village_door.gd hinge/prompt build_piece.gd cannot give it, so scripts/build/build_door.gd places it instead — see that entry's own `_comment_door`. Assets are the Medieval Village MegaKit subset docs/ASSET_LEDGER.md records for this item, matching the Plaster/UnevenBrick/RoundTile family EV6 is curating for the settlement itself (D24's one-family rule).
_comment_r2.7: R2.7. `workbench` is plain geometry, placed generically like the pieces above — GAME_DESIGN.md 19's 'at appropriate station' gating is a Rootstone-sink upgrade (spec 3 Band 2, SD18) that does not exist yet, so for now it is a physical marker, not a gate on crafting. `storage` is the second thing after `camp` that carries real state (its own inventory) and an interaction, so it gets its own hand-authored script the same way camp.gd does — see scripts/build/storage_container.gd. Both reuse assets EV7 already staged and ledgered (assets/props/quaternius_fantasy/), not new sourcing.
_comment_sd18_workbench_storage: SD18 looked at a Rootstone-funded `workbench`/`storage` upgrade and deliberately did NOT build one. `workbench` station-gating (crafting only working near a placed bench) does not exist in any form -- it would be new gating code (a location check on `craft()`, which is otherwise pure inventory arithmetic today), not a variant of something already here. `storage`'s inventory is `autoload/inventory.gd`'s own `SLOT_COUNT` (24), a class constant shared with the player's own satchel, not a per-instance capacity -- a bigger chest needs per-instance slot counts threaded through `storage_state.gd`/`storage_container.gd`/save data, also a new system. Both fail this item's own bar ('only if the existing buildables already support a variant cheaply'); GAME_DESIGN.md 32 bans a large crafting tree, and inventing either system to sink four recipes into a five-item tier is exactly that. Left for whichever item actually wants station-gated crafting or per-chest capacity as its own subject.
_comment_r2.8: R2.8. `creature_bed` is plain geometry, placed generically like `floor`/`wall`/`fence` above — GAME_DESIGN.md 16/20's full brief (revives a fainted creature, one per owned creature, visible creature rest behaviour) is R4.8's job once fainting/recovery exists; today this is a physical marker a player can place, the same scope R2.6/R2.7 shipped their own pieces at. Uses the Fantasy Props MegaKit's `Bed_Twin1`, staged for this item (docs/ASSET_LEDGER.md) rather than reusing `assets/props/quaternius_furniture/BedTwin.obj`, which is already the player's own bedroll/Grandpa's bed.
_comment_d34_categories: D34/spec section 12.2: the Valheim-style build menu's tabs are survival/crafting/structures/furniture, not this file's older shelter/structure/utility values (those were never read by anything before build_menu.gd). Remapped in place rather than adding a second field: tent/campfire/bedroll -> survival (they ARE the tutorial shelter, split three ways by OWNER-0902-CAMP-SPLIT), workbench -> crafting (the station crafting happens at), storage + creature_bed -> furniture (placed room contents, not load-bearing structure), floor/wall/door/roof/fence -> structures (literal building fabric). `thumbnail` is new: build_menu.gd's grid cells show only an image, never text (spec 12.3), so every entry needs one — see assets/ui/icons/buildables/ for how they were produced.
_comment_free: OF24, explicit owner directive: 'Torch building should be free.' No cost entries at all -- not cheap, free -- so lighting a camp was never blocked on materials. `mesh` was the same primitives-built prop the carried torch used (scripts/world/torch_prop.gd via scripts/player/torch.gd); `light` was read generically by scripts/build/build_piece.gd, not a torch-specific code path. SUPERSEDED by OW12 (owner, 2026-08-16: 'torches need to be a carry able item not placeable one') -- the `torch` entry this comment described is retired and no longer appears in the `buildables` array below. The torch is now `data/items/items.json`'s own `torch` entry, kind `tool`, equipped and carried the way an axe or pickaxe is. Left in place rather than deleted so this reversal of an explicit owner directive is legible to whoever reads this file next, not silently undone. See docs/decisions/D53.

buildables._comment_door: OP21-08. `door` used to be `Door_1_Flat.gltf` placed by build_piece.gd's generic mesh-plus-solid-box path -- a leaf mesh with no hinge, no Interactable, and a collider that sealed the opening it looked like it should open through. It also never cut a gap in a neighbouring `wall`, so a door beside a wall was purely decorative. It now composes the same three-module doorway every authored village cottage uses (data/config/building_prefabs.json's cottage_a/cottage_b recipes) and hangs the leaf on the real village_door.gd hinge -- see scripts/build/build_door.gd, which places this id instead of build_piece.gd (the same special-case path camp/storage/creature_bed already use for a reason build_piece.gd's generic mesh loader can't cover). `mesh` here is documentation only (matching `creature_bed`'s own entry below) -- build_door.gd hardcodes its own three module paths (WallGap/Frame/Leaf) rather than reading this field, the same way creature_bed.gd hardcodes `MESH_PATH` rather than reading its own `mesh` entry.

buildables.name: Roof
buildables.blurb: A round-tile roof panel to close a room in.
buildables._comment_scale: OP21-09. Measured Roof_RoundTile_2x1.gltf at 3.297w x 2.659h x 1.952d against the 2m module every other structural piece (floor/wall/door) is built on -- badly overhanging a 2x2 floor tile in width while depth was already close. scale.x/y = 2.0/3.297 = 0.6066 brings the footprint's worse-offending axis exactly onto the module (height follows width so the roof shrinks proportionally rather than flattening). BUILD-KIT-3: scale.z raised from 1.0 to 1.10 -- a blind critic ranked 'walls projecting past the roof' second of six defects (every reference building has eaves overhanging the wall plane; this kit's roof sat flush/inset instead). Z is the eave-to-eave axis (BLOCKED.md's open gable-cap item already established the ridge runs along local X), so scaling only Z adds overhang without touching the blocked mid-run seam or the X/Y module fit. scripts/build/build_snap_contract.gd::ROOF_Z_CENTER is this scale's own local-Z content centre (0.507180 * 1.10 = 0.557898) and MUST move with this number if it changes again -- it is not independently measured. Read generically by scripts/build/build_piece.gd's `model_scale` -- no code change per-mesh, and no new Meshy generation (CLAUDE.md hard rule).

buildables._comment_mesh: The camp set's bed -- but since the JUDGE-3 sec1d rework, creature_bed.gd COMPOSES the placed object (and its ghost) at runtime: this mesh becomes a squashed bedding pad inside a procedural canvas bolster ring. This key no longer builds the ghost (build_placer.gd instantiates creature_bed.gd for that, which composes the full nest); it still feeds the MENU THUMBNAIL, which therefore shows the plain camp bed rather than the composed nest -- a known, recorded mismatch until tools/render_build_thumbnails.gd learns to render composed pieces.
